Problem 1: Unsupervised City Pollution Profiles

Using multi-pollutant stoichiometric ratios, winter-to-monsoon seasonality amplitude, and severe frequency, Indian cities segment into 3 distinct atmospheric clusters explaining 79.15% of variance in the first two principal components.

Cluster 1

Gangetic High Smog Core

Cities: Delhi, Patna, Lucknow

Signature: Extreme winter thermal inversion, elevated PM2.5/PM10 ratio, high seasonal amplitude.

Cluster 2

Urban-Vehicular Coastal

Cities: Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Surat

Signature: Marine boundary layer dispersion, maritime breeze, moderate annual PM2.5 with NO2 spikes.

Cluster 3

Deccan & Semi-Arid Plateau

Cities: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad, Jaipur

Signature: Higher ventilation index, crustal coarse dust (PM10) dominance, low severe episodes.

Problem 3: Drivers of PM2.5 (Regression & Econometric Inference)

Quantifies the marginal effects of temperature, horizontal wind, boundary-layer stagnation, Diwali festive shock, and transboundary biomass plumes with City Fixed Effects and Cluster-Robust Standard Errors (R² = 0.858, Durbin-Watson = 1.914).
